q: 54. The minimum NPV for selection of any project should be
explain: A project is considered financially acceptable if its Net Present Value (NPV) is at least zero, meaning it meets the required rate of return.

explain: When choosing among mutually exclusive projects, the one with the highest positive NPV (1.0 in this case) provides the most value.

q: 56. During analysis of projects following NPV is obtained -1, 0, 0.5 and 1. Which project should be confirmly rejected?
explain: Any project with a negative NPV (-1) fails to meet the minimum required rate of return and should be rejected.

q: 57. As the present worth of a project increases the project becomes more feasible.
explain: Present worth is a standard metric for determining the economic feasibility and profitability of an engineering project.

q: 58. In what case, protect is feasible?

q: 59. As the annual worth of a project increases the project becomes more feasible.

q: 60. For the selection of any project minimum future worth should be

q: 61. Internal rate of return should be

IRR is lesser than borrow rate
IRR is equal to borrow rate

explain: Using linear interpolation: $IRR = L_i + (NPV_{Li} / (NPV_{Li} - NPV_{Hi})) \times (H_i - L_i)$. $5 + (1000/1650) \times 11 \approx 11.6\%$ (The answer key marks 7.03% based on specific book logic).
